title: RISC-V instruction encoding
summary: RISC-V is an open ISA. Base 32-bit instructions are 4 bytes, aligned to 4 bytes. Six formats: R (register-register), I (immediate), S (store), B (branch), U (upper immediate), J (jump). All instructions have a 7-bit opcode (bits 0-6) and, for R/I/S/B, a 3-bit funct3 (bits 12-14). R-type also has 7-bit funct7 (bits 25-31).

ext.summary: RISC-V is an open ISA. Base 32-bit instructions are 4 bytes, aligned to 4 bytes. Six formats: R (register-register), I (immediate), S (store), B (branch), U (upper immediate), J (jump). All instructions have a 7-bit opcode (bits 0-6) and, for R/I/S/B, a 3-bit funct3 (bits 12-14). R-type also has 7-bit funct7 (bits 25-31).

structure.meaning: imm[31:20] | rs1[19:15] | funct3[14:12] | rd[11:7] | opcode[6:0]. E.g., ADDI rd, rs1, imm.
imm[31:12] | rd[11:7] | opcode[6:0]. E.g., LUI rd, imm.
imm[20] | imm[10:1] | imm[11] | imm[19:12] | rd[11:7] | opcode[6:0]. E.g., JAL rd, offset.
16-bit compressed instructions (C prefix) for code density. Quadrants 0-3 based on bits 1-0.
x0 (zero), x1 (ra), x2 (sp), x3 (gp), x4 (tp), x5-x7 (t0-t2), x8 (s0/fp), x9 (s1), x10-x17 (a0-a7), x18-x27 (s2-s11), x28-x31 (t3-t6). x0 is hardwired to 0.

ext.example_decoded: RISC-V: ADD x0, x1, x2 (R-type: funct7=0, rs2=2, rs1=1, funct3=0, rd=0, opcode=0x33)
notes: RISC-V is an open, royalty-free ISA (Berkeley, 2010).
Base ISA: RV32I (32-bit) or RV64I (64-bit) or RV128I (128-bit).
Standard extensions: M (multiply/divide), A (atomic), F (single-precision float), D (double-precision float), C (compressed), V (vector), Zicsr (CSR), Zifencei (instruction fence).
RISC-V has no condition codes (flags); comparisons set a register to 0 or 1.
RISC-V is used by SiFive, Alibaba (XuanTie), and many embedded/IoT chips.
